statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

domain_restrictions: R(q) must be well-defined as a formal expression: [n choose l]_q ≠ 0 and division is interpreted in the ambient field/ring where Gaussian coefficients live (typically Q(q) or a localization of Z[q])
the premise “is a polynomial in q” means R(q) has no negative powers of q (i.e., R(q) ∈ coefficient_ring[q] for some coefficient ring)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Let n, k, l ∈ Z with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n. Define R(q) = [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q in the natural rational-function setting for Gaussian q-binomial coefficients. If R(q) lies in a polynomial ring in q (i.e., R(q) has only finitely many nonnegative powers of q with coefficients in the relevant coefficient ring), then when written as R(q) = Σ_i c_i q^i, every coefficient c_i satisfies c_i ≥ 0.
quantifier_order: for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n
if R(q) := [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q
then R(q) has only nonnegative coefficients

variables.name: n
variables.role: top index of Gaussian q-binomial coefficients; constrained by 0 ≤ k,l ≤ n (so effectively n ≥ 0)

variables.name: k
variables.role: middle index of first Gaussian q-binomial coefficient; constrained by 0 ≤ k ≤ n

variables.name: l
variables.role: middle index of second Gaussian q-binomial coefficient; constrained by 0 ≤ l ≤ n

variables.domain: formal (typically over a coefficient ring such as Z or Q)
variables.name: q
variables.role: variable with respect to which the ratio is required to be a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients

variables.domain: expression defined as ([n choose k]_q)/([n choose l]_q)
variables.name: R(q)
variables.role: the ratio whose membership in a polynomial ring and coefficient sign are being concluded
